# Cursor plugins

Official Cursor plugins for popular developer tools, frameworks, and SaaS products. Each plugin is a standalone directory at the repository root with its own `.cursor-plugin/plugin.json` manifest.

Author values match each plugin’s plugin.json author.name (Cursor lists plugins@cursor.com in the manifest).

Repository structure

This is a multi-plugin marketplace repository. The root .cursor-plugin/marketplace.json lists all plugins, and each plugin has its own manifest:

plugins/
├── .cursor-plugin/
│   └── marketplace.json       # Marketplace manifest (lists all plugins)
├── plugin-name/
│   ├── .cursor-plugin/
│   │   └── plugin.json        # Per-plugin manifest
│   ├── skills/                # Agent skills (SKILL.md with frontmatter)
│   ├── rules/                 # Cursor rules (.mdc files)
│   ├── mcp.json               # MCP server definitions
│   ├── README.md
│   ├── CHANGELOG.md
│   └── LICENSE
└── ...

aiSummary.oneLiner: Official, verified plugins to deeply integrate popular developer tools and workflows directly into the Cursor IDE.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: This repository serves as the official registry and codebase for plugins that extend the capabilities of the Cursor IDE and its internal AI agents. Each plugin is organized into its own standalone directory with a specific manifest, allowing users to integrate external services, documentation, and specialized workflows directly into their editor. The repository provides tools that give Cursor's agents direct access to resources like issue trackers, databases, and automated code review pipelines. It also includes scaffolding utilities so developers can rapidly build and validate their own custom plugins for proprietary internal systems.
keyFeatures: Verified integrations: Hosts official, vetted plugins connecting Cursor to major third-party developer tools.
Advanced workflow automation: Includes specialized agents for complex tasks like parallelized codebase auditing.
Custom plugin scaffolding: Provides CLI utilities to help developers quickly structure and test new, proprietary plugins.
Persistent agent memory: Supports plugins designed to continually update project guidelines and maintain long-term context.
Canvas visualization: Enables interactive rendering of complex architecture diagrams and API documentation within the IDE.

useCases.title: Extending editor context
useCases.description: Developers install plugins to give Cursor's AI agents direct, real-time access to external API documentation or issue trackers.

useCases.title: Automated branch reviews
useCases.description: Engineering teams deploy specialized workflow plugins to enforce strict security audits and code-quality rubrics before merging.

useCases.title: Internal tool integration
useCases.description: Enterprise users utilize the provided scaffolding to connect the IDE securely to their company's internal databases.

useCases.title: Continual project learning
useCases.description: Teams use memory-focused plugins to ensure the AI persistently updates and adheres to evolving project guidelines.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Software engineers, engineering teams, and enterprise developers using Cursor who need to tightly integrate their IDE with external services and proprietary workflows.
aiSummary.gettingStarted: Check the individual plugin directories in the repository for specific usage and installation instructions.
